name: BA15218 (ROHM dual low-noise, high-slew-rate bipolar)
tagline: ROHM's M5218-class dual op-amp (10 MHz GBW, 3 V/us). Japanese op-amp rollers say its highs sound cleaner and more extended than the M5218 or NJM4580.
technology: Monolithic dual op-amp with internal phase compensation, listed by ROHM as a low-noise, low-distortion, high-slew-rate part (bipolar; ROHM does not state the process in the search summaries). Runs from single 4-32 V or dual supplies. It is a consumer/audio catalogue part and is now end-of-life: the DIP8 version is obsolete, and the BA15218F-E2 had a Last Time Buy date of 2026-03-31.

part_numbers.notes: DIP8. DigiKey lists it as obsolete / no longer manufactured.
SIP8 (single-in-line). It will not fit a DIP8 op-amp socket. DigiKey and Mouser still have listings, but they do not show a lifecycle status.
SOP8. It is the only package covered by the 2013 TSZ-format datasheet and the ROHM product page.

part_numbers.status: Last Time Buy (LTB 2026-03-31 per distributor); effectively discontinued as of 2026-09
part_numbers.notes: Orderable tape-and-reel code for the BA15218F (DigiKey, Mouser, LCSC C79618). A marketplace suffix 'BA15218F-T1' also appears in listings but has not been confirmed by ROHM.

lineage.notes: Japanese low-noise dual op-amp with about 7 MHz GBW, per Japanese hobbyist sources. Unconfirmed from a vendor document.

lineage.period: legacy 'Standard ICs' catalogue (date unknown) through EOL (BA15218F-E2 LTB 2026-03-31)
lineage.notes: Japanese hobbyist sources describe it as ROHM's second source for the M5218 with GBW raised from about 7 to 10 MHz. The numbering follows ROHM's BA1xxxx pattern for second-sourced parts. The hobbyist claim has not been checked against a vendor document.

key_specs.value: 4 to 32 V single; +/-3 to +/-16 V dual (as summarized)
key_specs.source: ROHM legacy datasheet (alldatasheet 35931 / octopart mirror); the dual-supply lower limit is from a search summary and should be checked against the PDF

reputation.summary: This is a niche Japanese op-amp-rolling favourite, not a widely known audiophile legend. The C-Area wiki (atwiki) has a dedicated BA15218 listening page. In a comparison with the M5218 and NJM4580, the BA15218 was heard as having clean, open, extended highs, while the M5218 sounded slightly veiled and the NJM4580 had sluggish bass. A note.com headphone-amp write-up reports a firm, low-noise sound with solid lows. Another hobbyist comparison surfaced by search found it somewhat hard and less spacious than dedicated audio op-amps. All of these are single-listener subjective reports.
sonic_descriptors: somewhat hard, less spacious than audio-grade op-amps (one hobbyist comparison)
typical_uses: phono/RIAA and line stages (datasheet quotes RIAA noise)
op-amp rolling in headphone amps and DIY kits
caveats: EOL: the DIP8 BA15218 is obsolete, and the BA15218F-E2 LTB was 2026-03-31. Remaining supply is old stock or marketplace lots.
The BA15218N is SIP8 and the BA15218F is SOP8. Only the plain BA15218 drops into a DIP8 socket without an adapter.
The praise comes from a few Japanese hobbyist pages and is subjective. There are no measured audio comparisons.

counterfeit_notes: No documented counterfeit reports were found. Because the part is EOL, marketplace lots (e.g. Amazon '5PCS 15218 BA15218 BA15218F BA15218F-T1 BA15218F-E2 SOP8') are of unknown provenance, and remarked or reclaimed parts are a generic risk. Buy from authorised distributors while old stock lasts.
open_questions: Which ROHM PDN/EOL notice covers the BA15218F-E2 (LTB 2026-03-31)? TTI's ROHM PDN-1025006 came up in searches but has not been tied to this part.

corrections: Channel count corrected from 0 to 2 for all part numbers.
Packages added: BA15218 = DIP8, BA15218F = SOP8, BA15218N = SIP8.
Statuses filled in: BA15218 obsolete. BA15218F/-E2 EOL with Last Time Buy (LTB 2026-03-31). BA15218N unknown.
Added key_specs from the legacy ROHM datasheet (1.0 uVrms RIAA, 3 V/us, 10 MHz GBW, 0.5 mV VIO, 4-32 V single supply).
Added the current ROHM datasheet TSZ02201-0RAR1G200050-1-2 Rev.001 (10.SEP.2013) and legacy mirror copies.
Added lineage: hobbyist-reported M5218 second source / faster derivative.
Reputation softened to single-listener subjective reports. No silicon changes were found, so silicon_changes stays empty.
claims_confirmed: The legacy ROHM sheet 'Dual high slew rate, low noise operational amplifier' covers the BA15218/F/N and lists 4-32 V single / dual supply, Vn 1.0 uVrms (RIAA), SR 3 V/us, GBW 10 MHz and VIO 0.5 mV (https://www.alldatasheet.com/datasheet-pdf/pdf/35931/ROHM/BA15218.html).
Packages are DIP8 (BA15218), SOP8 (BA15218F) and SIP8 (BA15218N) (https://datasheet.octopart.com/BA15218-Rohm-datasheet-14139886.pdf).
The current ROHM datasheet is TSZ02201-0RAR1G200050-1-2, Rev.001, dated 10.SEP.2013 (https://fscdn.rohm.com/en/products/databook/datasheet/ic/amp_linear/opamp/ba15218f-e.pdf).

The ROHM product page shows the BA15218F-E2 as EOL announced / Last Time Buy (https://www.rohm.com/products/amplifiers-and-linear/operational-amplifiers/low-noise/dual-supply-voltage/ba15218f-product).
The BA15218F-E2 Last Time Buy date is 2026-03-31 per a distributor listing (https://www.digikey.co.uk/en/products/detail/rohm-semiconductor/BA15218F-E2/658252).
DigiKey lists the DIP8 BA15218 as obsolete (https://www.digikey.com/product-detail/en/rohm-semiconductor/BA15218/BA15218-ND/658251).
C-Area wiki listening notes: clearer, more open highs than the M5218 (slightly veiled) and NJM4580 (sluggish bass) (https://w.atwiki.jp/higemouse/pages/104.html).
A note.com headphone-amp BA15218 trial exists (https://note.com/jamjamjamw_w/n/n905ff5d7b92c).

Japanese hobbyist sources call the BA15218 ROHM's faster second source for the M5218 (GBW 7 to 10 MHz). This came from a search summary and the exact page was not pinned (https://w.atwiki.jp/higemouse/pages/104.html).
